fomc_decision.title: FOMC rate decision
fomc_decision.why: The single most-watched policy event on the calendar: market-implied probability of each decision bucket (cut, hold, hike) at the next scheduled FOMC meeting, from the exchange's highest-volume Fed series.
fomc_decision.source: Kalshi public API v2 — series KXFEDDECISION
fomc_decision.note: Buckets are mutually exclusive and use Kalshi's own wording; "Hike 0bps" means no change to the target range. If the meeting is canceled, the hold bucket resolves Yes.

measures.quantity: the size and direction of the change in the federal funds target range at the next scheduled FOMC meeting, in basis points — five mutually exclusive buckets (Cut >25bps, Cut 25bps, Hike 0bps, Hike 25bps, Hike >25bps)
measures.source_release: U.S. Federal Reserve — the FOMC statement (settlement source: federalreserve.gov)
measures.resolution: settles within minutes of the meeting statement on meeting day; a canceled meeting resolves the hold bucket to Yes — expected 2026-10-28
measures.text: the size and direction of the change in the federal funds target range at the next scheduled FOMC meeting, in basis points — five mutually exclusive buckets (Cut >25bps, Cut 25bps, Hike 0bps, Hike 25bps, Hike >25bps) Reference: October 28, 2026. Source: U.S. Federal Reserve — the FOMC statement (settlement source: federalreserve.gov). Resolution: settles within minutes of the meeting statement on meeting day; a canceled meeting resolves the hold bucket to Yes — expected 2026-10-28.

fomc_decision.paper: The paper finds the mode and median of the Kalshi distribution perfectly matched the realized federal funds rate on the day before every FOMC meeting since 2022 — a statistically significant improvement over fed funds futures (MAE 0.000 vs 0.010, RMSE 0.000 vs 0.020, p<0.05).

fed_funds.title: Fed funds rate level
fed_funds.why: The market's full policy-rate distribution: threshold probabilities for the funds-rate setting after the next FOMC meeting, complementing the decision buckets with the level the market actually prices.
fed_funds.source: Kalshi public API v2 — series KXFED
fed_funds.note: Each strike is the probability that the UPPER BOUND of the target range is strictly above that level following the meeting; strikes are cumulative, not mutually exclusive.

fed_funds.paper: The paper recommends Kalshi as the source for risk-neutral probability densities of FOMC decisions at specific meetings: fed funds futures force a two-outcome assumption, and SOFR options are too far removed (basis and horizon mismatch).

realized_track.note: Post-meeting target-range upper bound (4.00%), prevailing pre-meeting base 3.75% — per-meeting bases from the daily target-range series, never a single hardcode. Frozen at first observation.

cpi_yoy.title: CPI inflation (YoY)
cpi_yoy.why: Real-time inflation expectations between quarterly heat-map updates: the odds the headline CPI print clears each year-over-year threshold.
cpi_yoy.source: Kalshi public API v2 — series KXCPIYOY
cpi_yoy.note: Strikes are probabilities that YoY CPI prints strictly above each threshold ('more than X%', per the listed rules — an exact X.0 print resolves to No). The exchange sometimes lists a MoM market without the matching YoY market for a given print; those gaps are marked, never interpolated. No market was listed for the October 2026 print as of 2026-10-19 — the nearest listed market closes 2026-12-10. Gaps are marked, not interpolated.

measures.quantity: year-over-year CPI-U inflation for a named month — the one-decimal YoY rate over the twelve months ending that month; each strike is the probability the rate is strictly above the threshold
measures.source_release: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics — CPI news release (settlement source: bls.gov/cpi)
measures.resolution: settles on the release morning (trading closes 8:29 AM ET that day) on the BLS-reported one-decimal YoY value — expected 2026-12-10
measures.text: year-over-year CPI-U inflation for a named month — the one-decimal YoY rate over the twelve months ending that month; each strike is the probability the rate is strictly above the threshold Reference: November 2026. Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics — CPI news release (settlement source: bls.gov/cpi). Resolution: settles on the release morning (trading closes 8:29 AM ET that day) on the BLS-reported one-decimal YoY value — expected 2026-12-10.

cpi_yoy.paper: For headline CPI the paper finds Kalshi statistically significantly more accurate than the Bloomberg consensus: MAE 0.069 (mean) / 0.063 (median, mode) vs 0.081; RMSE 0.080 vs 0.100. For core CPI the two are statistically similar (MAE 0.070 both).

realized_track.note: YoY change in the NSA CPI-U index, one decimal — the quantity the contract settles on. Frozen at first observation (the index is not revised; the BLS computes YoY from unrounded indexes, so the last decimal can differ from the release table).

gdp_quarterly.title: GDP growth (quarterly)
gdp_quarterly.why: Growth-nowcast risk priced ahead of the release: odds that real GDP growth for the current quarter clears each threshold.
gdp_quarterly.source: Kalshi public API v2 — series KXGDP
gdp_quarterly.note: Strikes are probabilities that quarterly real GDP growth prints strictly above each threshold; strikes are not mutually exclusive. The event ticker embeds the release date (e.g. KXGDP-26OCT30) and the contract settles on the ADVANCE estimate.

measures.resolution: settles on the release morning (trading closes 8:29 AM ET that day) on the reported one-decimal rate — expected 2026-11-06

recession.title: NBER recession
recession.why: The clearest market summary of macro tail risk: the probability that a recession is underway within each covered window, on the technical-recession rule the contracts actually settle on.
recession.source: Kalshi public API v2 — series KXRECSSNBER
recession.note: Annual ladder: every open calendar-year market is charted. Despite the series ticker, the listed rules settle on BEA data — two consecutive quarters of negative real GDP growth within the covered window (2025 or 2026 for the 2026 market; Q4 2026 through Q4 2027 for the 2027 market) — NOT on NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee calls. Trading runs to the morning of the expected Q4 advance-GDP release (late January of the following year).

measures.quantity: whether a technical recession occurs within the covered window — the listed rule resolves Yes on two consecutive quarters of negative real GDP growth per BEA estimates; the series ticker says 'NBER' but settlement is the BEA two-quarter rule, not an NBER committee call
measures.reference: two consecutive negative real-GDP quarters within 2026: 2025Q1–2026Q4; 2027: 2026Q4–2027Q4
measures.source_release: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis — quarterly real GDP (advance estimates)
measures.resolution: closes at the sooner of occurrence or 8:25 AM ET on the expected release of the covered window's final Q4 advance-GDP estimate
measures.text: whether a technical recession occurs within the covered window — the listed rule resolves Yes on two consecutive quarters of negative real GDP growth per BEA estimates; the series ticker says 'NBER' but settlement is the BEA two-quarter rule, not an NBER committee call Reference: two consecutive negative real-GDP quarters within 2026: 2025Q1–2026Q4; 2027: 2026Q4–2027Q4. Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis — quarterly real GDP (advance estimates). Resolution: closes at the sooner of occurrence or 8:25 AM ET on the expected release of the covered window's final Q4 advance-GDP estimate.

recession.paper: Listed in the paper’s Table 1 as a Kalshi macro series; the paper’s calibration analysis finds the implied probability densities fairly well calibrated.

statuses.note: Exchange rule: two consecutive negative real-GDP quarters (BEA) within 2025Q1–2026Q4. Not occurred in the published estimates so far.
Exchange rule: two consecutive negative real-GDP quarters (BEA) within 2026Q4–2027Q4. Not occurred in the published estimates so far.

recession_realized.note: Realized overlay applies the exchange's own rule (two consecutive negative BEA quarters within the covered window — not NBER committee calls). GDP growth is the latest published estimate; flagged quarters are shaded where they fall in range.

ipo_pipeline.title: IPO pipeline
ipo_pipeline.why: A market-implied ECM pipeline gauge: the expected number of IPOs this year among the companies the exchange lists, plus the front-runners by announcement probability.
ipo_pipeline.source: Kalshi public API v2 — series KXIPO
ipo_pipeline.note: Each of the named company markets pays $1 if that company confirms an IPO before Jan 1, 2027 — confirmed means the SEC declares its Form S-1 effective, the IPO is priced, or an exchange assigns it a ticker (trading may start later). The window is calendar 2026; trading closes 11:59 PM ET on Dec 31, 2026. The expected count is the sum of the named companies' Yes prices, with already-confirmed companies counted at 1.0 each. The candidate set changes as companies are added or removed, so the count is a pipeline read, not a forecast.

tail_risks.title: Macro tail risks
tail_risks.why: Priced tail risk at a glance: the market-implied probability of high inflation prints and weak growth quarters, summed from the CPI and GDP strike ladders each day.
tail_risks.source: Derived from the CPI YoY and GDP series above (Kalshi public API v2)
tail_risks.note: Each series is the probability the outcome clears its threshold, read off the day's strike ladder. Marginal densities only: no joint probability of high inflation AND weak growth is measurable from these markets.
tail_risks.paper: Follows Figure 13 of the paper, which plots the same tail-risk time series; the paper stresses these are marginal densities.

measures.source_release: same releases as the CPI and GDP series (BLS CPI; BEA advance GDP estimate)
measures.resolution: inherits the underlying CPI and GDP events' resolution days
